summary: BlackFjord Capital — KV cache corruption during quantized kernel swap causing PII in completions (post-incident escalation)
description:
Issue summary:
During a rolling kernel swap for a quantized variant of redwood-llama-3-13b, KV cache entries were misrouted to an incompatible deserialization path. This caused a small percentage of completions to include tokens copied from unrelated customer requests. One BlackFjord request contained sensitive financial identifiers and partial SSN-like strings that were reflected back in another completion.

Impact:
- Customer: BlackFjord Capital (enterprise) experienced exposure of PII in 12 completions across a 27 minute window on 2026-03-10.
- Functional: Streaming completions truncated or interleaved with unrelated prompt fragments for ~0.05% of requests served by the affected pool.
- Business: Customer escalated to legal/security and paused traffic to the affected model for regulatory-sensitive workloads.

Environment:
- prod/us-east, dedicated pool serving enterprise tenants on redwood-llama-3-13b quant variants.
- Kernel swap triggered by automated rollout: kernel-selection service v3.12.1 -> v3.12.2.

Steps to reproduce (investigation method):
1) Synthetic load replay of customer traffic with preserved prompt fingerprints.
2) Force kernel-selection to swap to quant-int8 path while concurrent prefix lookups hit hot shards.
3) Observe mixed deserialization in KV lookup path; some entries decoded with legacy layout and appended into generation buffer.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Serving logs show KV lookup hits with mismatched schema tags: "kv:tag=0x6d" vs expected "0x72" around 2026-03-10T14:07:xxZ.
- Traces (trace IDs provided to customer) show a short window where kernel handshake allowed an incompatible kernel to be scheduled onto active workers.
- Grafana: token interleaving rate spike correlates with kernel-change posterior 14:05-14:32 UTC.
- Audit: No public S3 uploads contain PII; exposure limited to runtime memory and transient completions.

Mitigation performed during incident:
- Immediate rollback of kernel-selection to v3.12.1 across impacted pools (14:12 UTC).
- Invalidate and purge prefix/KV caches for affected GPU pool (14:14 UTC).
- Forced drain of in-flight connections on affected nodes and restarted serving processes (14:20-14:30 UTC).
- Rotated service-side signing keys for cache metadata to prevent reuse (14:45 UTC).
- Notified BlackFjord Security with full timeline and example traces; activated joint call and retained evidence package.

Resolution / customer-facing actions:
- Confirmed removal of affected entries and applied additional scrub to remove reproduced PII from logs and observability exports.
- Provided raw evidence and forensics export to BlackFjord under NDA; coordinated with their legal team.
- Issued a two-week credit for affected capacity and waived associated request charges during the incident window.
- Opened a cross-team remediation epic to prevent recurrence and improve test coverage.

Post-incident investigation summary (high level):
Root cause hypothesis: A non-atomic kernel swap path allowed a short interval where workers ran kernel binary A for compute but continued to use cache serialization schema from kernel binary B. Combined with a recent change to quantized serialization layout in v3.12.2, this produced misdecoded prefix entries that were appended to unrelated generation contexts.
Contributing factors:
- Lack of an end-to-end integration test for rolling kernel swaps with live cache schema variations.
- No guardrail to block schedule of newer kernel on nodes with cached legacy-encoded entries.

Next steps / action items:
- (ENG-1) Implement atomic kernel + cache-schema version gating; prevent non-backwards-compatible kernel from scheduling until cache invalidation completes.
- (ENG-2) Add end-to-end gating test in CI that simulates rolling kernel swaps with active prefix cache.
- (SRE-1) Create a dedicated alert for schema-mismatch tags in KV path; threshold tie to immediate rollout rollback.
- (DX-1) Update runbook and customer-facing incident template for any PII exposure with clear remediation checklist.
- (CS-1) Follow up with BlackFjord weekly until the remediation audit is accepted by their security team.

Attachments / evidence references: traces: trace-91a2f3, trace-91a2f4; grafana dashboard screenshot links were provided to customer on 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC.
